evals.prompt: Deploy this existing Next.js app to my production Temps context. Keep the current package manager and don't add unrelated dependencies.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the app and target context, runs the capability detector, offers missing observability once without blocking deployment, uses pinned @temps-sdk/cli with --target-context, and verifies deployment health.
expectations: Uses bunx or npx with @temps-sdk/cli@0.1.31 rather than a global temps command
Names an explicit target context for state-changing commands
Checks analytics, error tracking, and tracing before the final deploy step
Treats observability as an opt-in offer rather than a deployment requirement
Includes a read-only deployment verification

evals.prompt: Add Temps analytics and error tracking to this Vite React app, but do not enable session replay. I want proof both integrations send data.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the JavaScript how-to, preserves the package manager, proposes dependency/source changes, keeps credentials out of source, avoids replay, and verifies a synthetic analytics event and handled error end to end.
expectations: Loads only the React/JavaScript, analytics, error-tracking, and hygiene guidance
Does not enable session replay
Keeps the DSN environment-driven and avoids exposing server OTLP credentials
Verifies a synthetic analytics event and handled exception in Temps
Does not treat dependency installation as proof of delivery

evals.prompt: Show me the latest errors for project 42 in staging. Do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: Routes directly to the errors command reference, uses an explicit staging context and a pinned CLI invocation, performs only read operations, and does not load deployment or observability setup guides.
expectations: Uses only the relevant errors command-group reference
Uses @temps-sdk/cli@0.1.31 with the staging target context
Performs no state-changing operation
Does not offer instrumentation during a read-only error query

evals.prompt: Restore backup 0192 into the production Postgres database now. It is urgent.
evals.expected_output: Inspects immutable artifact and restore capabilities, explains source, recovery point, destination, overwrite and downtime, then obtains explicit confirmation immediately before any restore command.
expectations: Routes to backup-recovery and the focused backups/services command references
Does not treat urgency as authorization for a destructive restore
Names the explicit production target context and destination
Prefers a new isolated service when the user has not required in-place recovery
Requires engine-level structural verification before traffic changes

evals.prompt: Create a Redis service for project api in staging and wire its connection string into the app.
evals.expected_output: Inspects service types and existing resources, confirms staging context and service parameters, creates and links the service without exposing credentials, and verifies service health and linkage.
expectations: Routes to managed-services plus services command reference
Uses an explicit staging target context
Explains the write before execution
Never prints or persists the generated connection string
Verifies service health and project/environment linkage

evals.prompt: Add a GitHub Actions workflow that deploys this app to Temps production on pushes to main.
evals.expected_output: Creates a pinned, explicit-context CI workflow with secret-store credentials, preflight identity, bounded deployment verification, and no developer-local state.
expectations: Routes to ci-automation and deploy-application
Pins @temps-sdk/cli@0.1.31 and verifies the reviewed package integrity
Uses CI secrets rather than repository plaintext or local ~/.temps files
Uses an explicit production target context and preflight whoami
Waits for deployment health and fails on a bounded timeout
